Subject: Post-call: KMS/HSM questions + vendor security questionnaire

Hi Alan — thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end.

Recap of call:
- You asked about Redwood's encryption posture for data at rest and in transit, and whether we support customer-managed keys (BYOK).
- You also wanted to start a vendor security questionnaire and understand Redwood's SOC 2 / HIPAA posture.

Short answers:
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mTLS available for private deployments.
- Encryption at rest: All persisted model artifacts and request logs are encrypted. For hosted customers we provide service-managed encryption by default.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. We integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support HSM-backed CMKs.
- SOC / HIPAA / GDPR: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in 2024. We offer BAA for HIPAA-covered workloads and have regional data residency options for GDPR concerns.

Attachments I’m sharing here for your team to review:
- Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf (high-level controls and SOC 2 attestation summary)
- Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (our template to speed the exchange)
- KMS_Integration_Spec.pdf (technical details on CMK modes and key flow)

Proposed next steps:
1) If you can, put security@lumenhealth on the thread and send over your vendor questionnaire — we’ll fill it and return within 3 business days.
2) Engineering sync: propose Thu Jan 22 at 10:00 AM PT or Fri Jan 23 at 9:00 AM PT for a short technical call (30 min) to walk the key lifecycle and HSM options.
3) If you need a BAA, I can loop in Legal — we typically surface a draft after the questionnaire.

Let me know which time works and I’ll calendar.

Thanks,
— Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our security team before we schedule the call: 

1) BYOK model specifics: Does Redwood support customer CMKs that are CloudHSM-backed (AWS CloudHSM / CloudKMS with CloudHSM root)? Can the CMK remain under our control (we hold the CMK and Redwood only receives encrypted data keys)?
2) Envelope encryption: Do you use envelope encryption and can you describe how DEKs/KEKs are managed?
3) Key rotation and access: Is automatic rotation supported and is rotation audit logged so we can tie usage to CloudTrail/events?
4) HSM assurance: Are the HSMs FIPS 140-2/FIPS 140-3 validated? For on-prem HSMs, do you support integration with our existing Thales appliances?
5) Logging/forensics: Can we get cryptographic usage logs (key ID, operation, timestamp) for forensic purposes?

We’ll upload our standard vendor questionnaire; I’m copying security@lumenhealth.

Also attaching a short doc with our compliance expectations (Lumen_Vendor_Intro.docx).

If you prefer, we can discuss the above on the call — would still like to get a brief written confirmation on these points first.

Subject: Re: Post-call: KMS/HSM questions + vendor security questionnaire

Alan — great questions. High-level confirmations below; I’ve looped Neha (Security) and Vivek (Platform) for any deeper tech notes or follow-up.

- BYOK and CMKs: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed CMKs. Two common modes: (1) Cloud KMS integration where a customer CMK (KMS key) lives in your cloud account and Redwood calls KMS APIs to perform DEK wrap/unwrap, and (2) HSM-backed CMKs (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM) where the root key material is held in the HSM. In both cases Redwood does not retain plaintext CMKs.
- Envelope encryption: We use envelope encryption. Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) are generated per-customer/tenant, encrypted with the KEK/CMK, and the encrypted DEK is stored.
- Rotation & audit: Key rotation is supported and can be managed via your KMS (we respect rotation policies). Key usage events that occur in the customer KMS appear in your cloud audit logs (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs). Redwood emits operational logs that indicate key-id references (not plaintext keys) which we can forward to your SIEM on request.
- HSM validation & Thales: Cloud-hosted HSMs (CloudHSM) meet common compliance controls; for Private/on-prem we can integrate with Thales/Entrust appliances — we’ve done this with customers. Specific FIPS attestations depend on the HSM vendor/model; we can provide proof-of-compliance artifacts for the platform-backed HSMs.
- Logs/forensics: We provide metadata for crypto ops (key id, op type, timestamp) in our audit logs. Full KMS usage logs come from your KMS.

I’ve attached a short KMS integration spec with diagrams (KMS_Integration_Spec.pdf) and our security overview.

Proposed times again for the engineering sync: Thu Jan 22 at 10:00 AM PT (preferred) or Fri Jan 23 at 9:00 AM PT. Which works for your team?

If it helps, Vivek can run the technical call and walk through our key lifecycle flow live.

Thanks,
— Soojin
Soojín Lee
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: KMS/HSM questions + vendor security questionnaire

Quick tech notes from platform: 
- Envelope encryption: We generate per-tenant DEKs; DEKs are wrapped with the customer’s CMK. Wrapped DEKs are stored with the tenant metadata.
- CMK control: In cloud-KMS mode the CMK lives in the customer account; we only get wrapped DEKs and call KMS/CloudHSM APIs for unwrap ops. In Private deployments where we operate in the customer VPC, we can route key calls to your HSM.
- Rotation: Supported via your KMS rotation policy; when a rotation happens, we will re-wrap new DEKs as needed.
- HSM FIPS/assurance: For cloud HSMs, customers can request HSM attestation artifacts (we will share our standard references). For on-prem integrations we work with your security team to validate model-level FIPS status.
- Audit logs: Our runtime logs key-id references. For complete cryptographic audit trails, leverage your KMS/CloudHSM logs (CloudTrail). We can also send operational traces to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with hashed key identifiers for correlation.

Happy to demo the flow on Thu Jan 22 if that time is confirmed.

— Vivek

Senior Platform Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
